title: Make your compliance repo
summary: Install hound, make your organisation's private compliance repo with hound init, and onboard a supplier and a system with your agent drafting and you approving.

steps.title: Everything about you lives in one private repo
narration: CISO Assistant is your system of record. Your compliance repo is how you configure it.
It is a private git repository that holds your scope, your mappings, your suppliers and your collector settings.
Every change goes in as a commit, so you can see who changed what, and roll it back.
Secrets never go in it. They stay on the server, and the repo names them only by reference.

panel.title: In the repo, and never in it
lines: In: hound.yaml, scope/, mappings/, supplier files, manual evidence runbooks
Never: passwords, API tokens, certificates and keys, exported evidence, .env files

steps.title: Install hound
narration: On your laptop, install hound as a .NET tool, from the release's packages.
Give the version, so you get the one you meant.
Then check it answers.

steps.title: Start the repo with hound init
narration: hound init asks about your organisation: its name, a short code, your CISO Assistant address, your time zone, the maturity level you aim for, and who owns compliance.
It writes the config, the scope and the Essential Eight mapping, and checks them.
Each system you onboard later gets its own audit, so the gaps show per system.
Your turn: start a repo called my-compliance for Example Pty Ltd.

terminal.output:
Short code for ref IDs [EX]:
CISO Assistant address [https://ciso.example.com]:
Time zone [Australia/Sydney]:
Essential Eight maturity level [2]:
Who owns compliance (email): grc@example.com

try.prompt: Type the command that starts a repo called my-compliance for Example Pty Ltd.

steps.title: Commit it, and set up your agent
narration: Make it a git repository and commit the first version.
Then run hound agent setup for the assistant you use, Claude Code or GitHub Copilot.
It writes skills that teach your agent every hound command and every workflow, so it drafts the way hound expects.
Push the repo to a private repository on your git host.

terminal.command: cd my-compliance && git init -b main && git add . && git commit -m "Start from hound init"

terminal.output: Wrote the skills and agents for Claude Code.

steps.title: The agent drafts a supplier
narration: Onboarding goes in a fixed order: the organisation, then its suppliers, then each system.
Give your agent the vendor's documents and ask it to draft the supplier.
It records each risk level with a reason, and writes a draft contract and an open review.
Nothing is approved yet. A draft waits for you.

terminal.command: hound supplier draft --system GRC-PLATFORM --ref SUP-ORACLE --name "Oracle Cloud Infrastructure" --solution-ref SOL-OCI-HOSTING --solution-name "OCI compute, networking and storage" --contract-ref CTR-OCI-2026 --contract-name "OCI pay-as-you-go 2026" --level "dependency=3:The GRC platform runs only on it." --kind vendor --json

steps.title: The agent onboards a system, one requirement at a time
narration: Next, the system. The agent starts a session with the system's owner, product and supplier.
Then it decides each requirement and says how it is met: an API check, manual evidence, another system, or not applicable.
Every decision carries its reasoning, and the source it rests on.
When pending lists nothing, the system is ready for you.

terminal.command: hound onboard GRC-PLATFORM pending --json --repo . --group 1 --group 2 --owner it@example.com --product "GRC platform" --solution SOL-OCI-HOSTING
hound onboard GRC-PLATFORM decide ISM-1515 --repo . --json --kind manual --reasoning "A quarterly restore test to a scratch VM, recorded in the restore log."

choice.question: The agent marks a requirement not applicable because the system has no privileged users. What happens next?

options.text: It is out of the audit at once.
options.feedback: Not yet. A not-applicable decision an agent drafted always waits for a person.

options.text: It waits for you to read its reasoning and approve it.
options.feedback: Yes. An assessor will ask why, so a person signs every not-applicable decision.

steps.title: You approve, in your own terminal
narration: Now run hound approve. It needs a person at a terminal, and refuses when an agent runs it.
It walks you through each draft, one at a time: the supplier first, then the system and its decisions.
Answer y, n to leave it as a draft, or s to stop.
Your turn: type the command that approves the drafts in this repo.

terminal.output:
Your name, recorded with today's date on everything you approve: Sam Example
[supplier] SUP-ORACLE Oracle Cloud Infrastructure: contract CTR-OCI-2026 is a draft.
Approve it? (y, n, s): y

try.prompt: Type the command that approves the drafts in this repo.

steps.title: Check the plan, then apply
narration: Approving changes files in the repo, and nothing in CISO Assistant yet.
Validate the scope, then plan, and read the plan: it lists every object and field the apply would write.
Apply writes exactly that saved plan, and a second plan shows nothing new.
From now on, each change goes in as a pull request, and the plan is what reviewers approve.

terminal.command: hound scope plan scope --config hound.yaml --out scope.plan.json
terminal.output:
+ third party SUP-ORACLE Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
+ asset GRC-PLATFORM
+ audit EX-E8-Q2-2027FY-GRC-PLATFORM
Plan saved to scope.plan.json.
